description: Golden vectors shared by the Python data checks and the JVM tests for the pure NVIDIA core. Hex values are strings; sizes are decimal; vramMiB 0 means the adapter reported no memory.
notes: This PC: RTX 5080 LUID ending e782 (physical, owns the display), GameViewer twin LUID ending b95ad (virtual, ROOT enumerated), AMD iGPU, software adapter.

Only the LUID suffixes e782 and b95ad, the 5080 identity (10DE:2C02 subsystem 8A4A1043 revision A1, 15978 MiB, driver 32.0.16.1742) and the PnP prefixes were measured. The LUID high parts, the AMD ids and LUID, the software adapter LUID and the PnP instance tails are fixture placeholders.
Several device ids for real products (marked pciTable unknown) are intentionally absent from the Kotlin PCI table: the name decides, and the table is only a secondary source.
Hypothetical names (RTX 5080 SUPER, RTX 6090) exist only to exercise the base-model and unknown-base rules.

gpus.description: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition

scenarios.note: RTX 5080 physical e782 first, AMD iGPU, GameViewer twin b95ad, software adapter. Pin safe, no cross-adapter.
Same inventory, the display adapter is not known: no cross-adapter step-down.
The virtual twin enumerates first: the first NVIDIA prefix match is the twin, so the pin is unsafe.
Only the virtual twin, AMD and software adapters: hard decline.
No NVIDIA adapter at all.
Only the software adapter.
A complete but empty inventory is Absent.
DXGI incomplete with the twin in the partial list: Unknown, never accepted.
DXGI failed outright: Unknown, not Absent.
The PnP query failed for both identical adapters: ambiguous, hard decline.
The PnP query failed but only one adapter has that PCI identity: accepted with a note.
The twin is verified virtual but the real card's PnP query failed: identity is shared, so decline.
The only RTX owns no output (the iGPU drives the display): one tier down.
The monitor belongs to the AMD adapter: one tier down.
Laptop 5080 whose display is on the iGPU: ULTRA, minus mobile, minus cross-adapter.
Two physical GPUs: the one with an attached output wins over the stronger one.
Neither owns an output: the higher class wins (then cross-adapter, one tier down).
Both own an output; the adapter that owns the video window's display beats the stronger one.
A non printable-ASCII description cannot be pinned exactly: the legacy literal, still safe when first.
With a legacy pin the first NVIDIA prefix match is the twin: unsafe.
A virtual-sounding name only excludes: this adapter has a PCI path yet is not accepted.
A virtual-named adapter first does not break the exact pin: its description is not a prefix match.
A pre-RTX GPU alone is a hard decline but keeps a pin for decode steering.
This PC's card with a pre-572.16 driver: DRIVER_OLD.
Ada card with a 550.00 driver: allowed, advisory not triggered, HDR gate closed.
